title: SLA tolerance matrix for GPU preemption and cross-region failover
creator: Nisha Patel
description: Define a measurable SLA/SLO tolerance matrix and acceptance criteria to cover two linked failure modes: (1) transient GPU preemption events in Dedicated pools that cause short-term throughput loss and (2) automated cross-region failover when regional capacity is degraded. This ticket establishes latency bands, per-tenant error budget charging rules for preemption-induced errors, canary rollback thresholds, and the gated rollout plan for Hosted + Dedicated + Private deployments. The goal is to provide clear, testable contracts for product, SRE, and sales teams so we can safely enable automated cross-region failover and preemption-aware routing without regressing customer-facing latency and availability.
background: We observed multiple incidents where EC2/GCP GPU preemptions caused brief but significant p99 tail latency spikes and request failures. Current regional failover behavior is conservative and requires manual intervention; we want an automated policy for cross-region failover with explicit SLOs and safe gates. This PRD complements ENG work on more graceful preemption handling (ENG-61220) and per-tenant throttling policies (ENG-60789).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented SLA tolerance matrix that defines acceptable availability and latency bands for: a) normal operation, b) during GPU preemption events, and c) during cross-region failover. 2) Numeric SLOs established: p50/p90/p99 token latency envelopes per model class and per region; availability SLOs per tenant class (Standard, Premium). 3) Error budget accounting rules: preemption-induced 5xx vs regional routing failures must be classified and charged differently; explicit formula documented. 4) Canary release guardrails: canary burn rate thresholds and probe metrics defined so automated canary can be aborted at specific burn rates. 5) Runbook and rollout checklist created and linked. 6) Dashboards and alerting queries added for adoption (linked). 7) Stakeholder sign-off from SRE, Runtime eng, Sales Ops, and Legal for SLA guarantees.
success_metrics: - Reduction in manual failover incidents by 80% in the quarter after rollout. - No more than 10% increase in tenant-facing p99 tail during controlled preemption simulations. - Canary aborts triggered at or before the defined burn-rate thresholds in at least 95% of test runs. - Accurate billing attribution: per-tenant error budget logs show preemption-classified events separated from platform faults.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Finalize tolerance matrix and acceptance criteria (this ticket). Phase 1: Implement monitoring/metrics and offline simulation run (staging) with synthetic preemption events. Phase 2: Small canary (1% traffic) with weighted tenants in a non-peak regional window; gate on burn-rate and p99 probe metrics. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with automated rollback policy. Phase 4: Post-rollout review and SLA update for affected customers. Each phase has an explicit go/no-go checklist and ownership allocated to Runtime and SRE.
implementation_notes: - Need a classification tag for preemption-induced failures at the runtime layer so chargeback logic can distinguish root cause. - Runtime change required to surface preemption reason codes in spans (ENG-61220). - Billing/usage metrics team to add a dimension for 'failure_reason' for error budget attribution. - Coordinate timing windows with Sales Ops for Premium tenants and scheduled maintenance windows.
risks: - Misclassification of failure cause could lead to incorrect SLA credits. - Rolling out cross-region failover may increase inter-region egress costs. - Canary may be noisy for bursty tenants; need tenant weighting to avoid high-impact customers in early canaries.
decisions: 1) Use weighted-tenancy canary composition: include at least one Premium and two Standard tenants in every canary. 2) Preemption events under 30s are treated as 'transient' and go into a separate error bucket; >=30s considered 'regional degradation'. 3) Initial automated failover will prefer warm-warm region pairs to minimize cold-starts.

notes: This ticket intentionally separates classification of root cause (preemption vs platform fault) to avoid overcharging the platform's error budget for third-party transient events. We will run two rounds of simulated preemptions with archived traces to validate classification heuristics before canary.
